meta.title: Social Organizer: a network of people you know
meta.description: A network of people who know each other in person. When someone is in trouble, many can help.

hero.title: Your circle is bigger than you think.
hero.lead: Social Organizer brings together people who know each other in person. When someone is in trouble, their acquaintances hear about it first, then the people those acquaintances know.

story.sceneAria: A flock of starlings: each bird stands for a person in the network

b1.label: Starlings
b1.say: A starling keeps track of only six or seven neighbours, yet a flock of thousands flies as one.

b2.say: People are connected the same way.
b2.stat: handshakes separated two random Facebook users on average in 2016: fewer than four people in between. <study>The study</study>

b3.label: 1 · A network of people you know
b3.say: You invite someone you know in person, and you both confirm you know each other.
b3.late: Then they invite people they know.

b4.label: 2 · A Need
b4.say: Say Sarah has lost her job and the rent is due in a week. She's {{shortfall}} short.
b4.late: Sarah reports a Need and adds a link to a chat. A {{shortfall}} Need reaches up to {{reach}} people, nearest first.

b5.label: 3 · Everyone decides for themselves
b5.say: You know Tom, and Tom knows Sarah. You can see this chain and ask Tom what happened.
b5.late: Whether to take part is your choice.

b6.label: 4 · A little from many
b6.say: Anyone willing to take part names an amount from {{min}}. You name {{mine}}.
b6.late: It's an intention, and nothing is paid now. While the Need is open, you can change the amount or withdraw.

b7.label: 5 · People agree directly
b7.say: Sarah and the participants talk it over in the chat. Emma says the shop where she works is hiring.
b7.late: If money is involved, people hand it over themselves. The app never touches it.

b8.label: You
b8.say: Tomorrow it could be you in Sarah's place.
b8.late: Then the people you know will be the first to hear about your Need.

b9.label: In the app
b9.say: This is how your network looks in the app: you in the middle, the people you know around you, the people they know further out.
b9.late: When someone needs help, you see the chain of acquaintances from them to you.

faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: Who makes sure people keep their word?
faq.a1: There are no middlemen. You decide whom to trust and deal with people directly, and through the chain of acquaintances you can find out who you're dealing with.
faq.q2: Is this insurance or a fund?
faq.a2: No. Nobody pays in advance and nobody promises a payout. There's no common pot and no treasurer.
faq.a3: No. A Need reaches only people linked to its author through acquaintances, and next time you may be the one who asks.
faq.a4: No. Nobody pays to join and nobody earns from invites.
faq.a6: We keep account and profile details, including your name, email, sign-in account identifiers and anything you add, such as a photo, phone number or location. We keep your settings (such as language and theme), invitation and connection history, reported Needs, Participation and the amounts you name. We also keep sign-in codes, push tokens and notification history, and any complaints or support messages you send. The app never touches money and asks for no card or bank details.

meta.title: How it works — Social Organizer
meta.description: You build a network of people you know. A Need reaches as many people in it as the dollars it names, and participants coordinate directly. The page also compares Social Organizer with China’s online mutual aid platforms.

hero.title: First the network, then the signals
hero.lead: Social Organizer starts with a network of people you know in person. Two signals travel through it. With a Need, a participant says what they need. With a Participation, another participant says they will take part and names an amount. People agree on the rest and do it themselves.

orbit.title: How far a message travels
orbit.lead: Your friends know their own, and a Need travels by handshakes. It reaches those who have a path to you through people they know, and everyone decides for themselves.
says: Six people you know. This is the circle: people you have confirmed you know.
Each of the six has their own six. 36 people you do not know, but someone of yours does.
One more step gives 216 people. The message reaches them too, through those who know you.
orbit.sumNote: if everyone named {{share}}. A simplified example: in life circles overlap, and nobody has to take part

chain.title: A path through people you know
chain.lead: A Need reaches as many people as it names dollars, the nearest by handshakes first. You only see Needs that have a path to you through people you know. Tap a person.
says: Maria Koval reports a Need. You do not know her.
Oleg, your brother, knows Maria. That is why he receives her message.
You receive the message because you know Oleg. You decide whether to take part.

join.title: It starts with a person you know
join.lead: The network grows only through people who know each other: someone joins by your link, and you confirm the acquaintance.
says: Katya opens your link and signs in. This is not a connection yet: you get a push.
You confirm: yes, we know each other. Now Katya is your 1st handshake.

cta.title: Start with people you already know

compare.title: The closest example: China’s online mutual aid
compare.lead: From 2018 to 2021 China’s online mutual aid platforms gathered hundreds of millions of members: the largest, Xianghubao, had over 100 million. Members shared the cost of each other’s serious illness, a few dollars a year each. In 2021 regulators closed the whole sector, because each platform’s operator was in effect running insurance.
compare.note: Social Organizer keeps their idea: when one person has a hard time, many people each take a small part. It has no operator and no pot.
compare.caption: China’s online mutual aid platforms compared with Social Organizer
rows: Nobody: a network of people who know each other
As many people as the Need names dollars, nearest first
The platform, and with it everything
There is no pot and no payouts to shut down

how.groupsLink: Bringing your group? How to start together

meta.title: For groups — Social Organizer
meta.description: How to bring your group into Social Organizer together: why a group starts faster than one person, the first steps, and texts to copy into your group chat.

hero.title: Bring your group in together
hero.lead: Your group already stands by its own people. In Social Organizer, when one of you reports a Need, the people that person knows hear about it first, then the people they know: up to one person for each dollar still needed.

why.title: Why start as a group
why.lead: To report a Need, you need {{direct}} people in your circle who have confirmed they know you, and {{network}} people in your network, counted to the 6th handshake. Your circle counts in your network; you don't.
why.alone: Both counts start at zero, and you wait for each person you know to join.
why.group: If {{n}} of you join and each confirms {{direct}} others from the group, every one of you can report a Need the same day.

own.title: Your group keeps its own way
own.lead: Whatever your group calls itself, a chama, a paluwagan or a church group, its own way stays: your meetings, your rules, your treasurer.
own.text1: Social Organizer holds no money, has no pot and takes no fee. When someone reports a Need, each of you decides alone whether to take part, from $1. While the Need is open, you can change the amount or withdraw.
own.text2: The author of the Need and the participants agree in their own chat, in any messenger. Money, if any, goes directly between people.

steps.title: How to start
steps.s1: Install the app and sign in. Open “{{add}}” and send your link to the group chat with “{{share}}”.
steps.s2: Each person who opens your link and taps “{{known}}” comes to you. Confirm the people you know in person.
steps.s3: Meet once. In the app, one of you opens “{{myQr}}” and the other taps “{{scan}}”. A live code confirms the acquaintance at once, so in one evening each of you can confirm {{direct}} others.
steps.s4: Each of you sets “{{stake}}”: the amount you are usually ready to give when someone in the network is in trouble. Then invite the people you know outside the group.

texts.invite: I've joined Social Organizer. People who know each other in person build a network there. If one of us reports a Need because of a job loss or urgent surgery, the people who know that person hear first, then the people they know. No money goes through the app. Join through my link, and I'll confirm that we know each other: {{link}}
texts.explain: Social Organizer brings together people who know each other in person. When one of us reports a Need, each person decides whether to take part, from $1, and any money goes directly between people. {{link}}
texts.confirm: To everyone who has joined: to report a Need, each of us needs 5 confirmed acquaintances and 10 people in the network. Post your own link here (“{{add}}” → “{{share}}”). Open the links of people you know in person and tap “{{known}}”. When someone comes through your link, confirm them. At our next meeting we can do it faster: “{{myQr}}” and “{{scan}}”.

honest.title: Tell your group plainly
list: A Need may not be covered. Each person decides alone.
Nobody gets a rating. People in your network see two numbers: how often someone reported Participation, and how often authors marked it as received.

meta.title: Press kit — Social Organizer
meta.description: What Social Organizer is, who makes it, the main facts, the logo and screenshots to download, and how to reach the team.

hero.title: Press kit
hero.lead: In Social Organizer people build a network of those they know in person: you add someone you know, and you both confirm it. When one of you is in trouble, that person reports a Need. For a shortfall of {{need}}, up to {{reach}} people hear about the Need, starting with the closest connections in the network. Each person sees who links them to the author and decides whether to take part. Anyone willing names an amount from {{min}}. It's an intention, not a payment. People agree in their own chat and hand over any money themselves; the app never touches it.

del.lead: You delete your account yourself, from inside it: in the app, on the website or in the Telegram Mini App. No e-mails and no waiting.
del.step1: Open the app, orginizer.com or the Telegram Mini App and sign in
del.cta: Sign in and delete the account
del.gone1: Profile: name, photo, phone, e-mail, contacts
del.gone2: Sign-in methods: Telegram, Google, Apple, password
del.gone4: Your open Needs and your Participation in open Needs
del.gone5: Notifications, push subscriptions, settings, chats with the assistant
del.whenText: Deletion is immediate and cannot be undone. If you had connections, other people’s networks keep “Deleted user” in place of your name, with no personal data. Past Needs of other people keep the amounts without your name.
del.noAccessText: Accounts are deleted only from inside the account; there is no deletion by request. If you can’t sign in, the profile is deleted automatically after 2 years without sign-ins. We warn 30 and 7 days before that through Telegram, push notifications and e-mail, whichever the account has.

policy.s1: Social Organizer ("we", "our", "the service") is an open-source coordination tool: it carries participants’ messages about Needs and voluntary Participation. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, and protect your personal data when you use the app, our Telegram Mini App and the website at orginizer.com.
policy.s2a: Account data: name, email address, Telegram user ID and username (when logging in via Telegram).
policy.s2b: Profile data: photo, contact information you choose to add (social links, phone number).
policy.s2c: Network data: your connections with other users, invitation history.
policy.s2d: Activity data: Needs you report, your Participation, the amounts you name, and your intention.
policy.campaigns: We count landing page visits and button clicks by day, campaign tags and the referring site's hostname. The counters use no cookies or visitor identifiers. First-touch campaign tags may stay on your device for up to 30 days and are saved to your account when you sign up.
policy.s3a: To run the service: to show you the network of people you know.
policy.s3b: To carry messages about Needs and Participation across your network.
policy.s3c: To send notifications about Needs, invitations, and network activity.
policy.s3d: To improve the App based on aggregated, anonymized usage patterns.
policy.s4lead: We do not sell your personal data. Your data is shared only with:
policy.s4a: Your network members: your name, photo, and contact info you choose to make visible.
policy.s4b: Telegram: data necessary for the Mini App to function within Telegram.
policy.s4c: Hosting providers: our servers process your data to deliver the service.
policy.s5: Your data is stored in a secure PostgreSQL database. We use encrypted connections (HTTPS/TLS), JWT-based authentication, and follow industry-standard security practices to protect your information. Accounts with no sign-ins for 2 years are deleted automatically, after notices 30 and 7 days in advance.
policy.s6a: Access your personal data through your profile and settings.
policy.s6b: Correct or update your information at any time.
policy.s6c: Delete your account and associated data yourself in Profile → Account.
policy.s6d: Export your data in a machine-readable format.
policy.s7: Social Organizer is fully open source. You can review our codebase and how your data is handled at <gh>github.com/element1965/Social-organizer</gh>.
policy.s8: For questions about this Privacy Policy or your data, contact us via <bot>Telegram</bot>.
policy.s3e: To decide who receives a Need first: we count how often you open and answer such messages, and how many you got lately. These counts are never shown to anyone and used for nothing else.

termsDoc.s1: Social Organizer is a free, open-source coordination tool. It records two kinds of participant messages, a Need and a voluntary Participation, and notifies people about them. The service is available in the app, as a Telegram Mini App and at orginizer.com.
termsDoc.s2: By using Social Organizer, you agree to these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, please do not use the App.
termsDoc.s3a: You must provide accurate information when creating an account.
termsDoc.s3b: You are responsible for maintaining the security of your account.
termsDoc.s3c: You may create only one account per person.
termsDoc.s3d: You must be at least 16 years old to use the service.
termsDoc.s4a: Confirm that they know each other through personal invitations.
termsDoc.s4b: Report a Need and their own voluntary Participation.
termsDoc.s4d: Discover connection paths between network members.
termsDoc.s5a: Report invented Needs or mislead other people.
termsDoc.s5b: Misrepresent your identity or relationship to others.
termsDoc.s5c: Use the service for illegal activities or spam.
termsDoc.s5d: Attempt to exploit, hack, or disrupt the service.
termsDoc.s6: Social Organizer is a coordination tool, not a financial institution, a fund or a payment intermediary. The service does not accept, transfer, hold or distribute funds. A Participation is a participant’s voluntary intention; it is not a payment. Participants may agree to hand over money or to help in another way: such arrangements and actions take place directly between them, outside the service. Amounts and received marks are entered by participants themselves; the service does not verify them. We do not guarantee that assistance will be given and are not responsible for whether participants keep their arrangements.
termsDoc.s7: The service is provided "as is" without warranties of any kind. We are not liable for any damages arising from the use of the service, including but not limited to financial losses from arrangements between participants that were not kept.
termsDoc.s8: Social Organizer is open-source software licensed under its repository terms. The source code is available at <gh>github.com/element1965/Social-organizer</gh>.
termsDoc.s9a: Social Organizer has a zero-tolerance policy toward child sexual abuse and exploitation (CSAE). We strictly prohibit any content, behavior, or use of the service that sexually exploits or endangers minors in any way.
termsDoc.s9lead: Specifically, the following are strictly forbidden:
termsDoc.s9b: Sharing, distributing, or soliciting child sexual abuse material (CSAM) of any kind.
termsDoc.s9c: Grooming, trafficking, or exploitation of minors.
termsDoc.s9d: Any communication of a sexual nature with or about minors.
termsDoc.s9e: Using the service to facilitate access to children for harmful purposes.
termsDoc.s9f: Users must be at least 16 years of age. We reserve the right to immediately terminate accounts and report violators to the appropriate law enforcement authorities, including the <ncmec>National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC)</ncmec> and local law enforcement.
termsDoc.s9g: If you encounter any content or behavior that violates these standards, please report it immediately via <bot>Telegram</bot>.
termsDoc.s10: We may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of the App after changes constitutes acceptance of the new terms.
termsDoc.s11: For questions about these Terms, contact us via <bot>Telegram</bot>.
termsDoc.s6b: Amounts in the service are stated in US dollars as a common unit of account. Which currency and which way to use is decided between participants.

s1.title: You are at the centre of your circle
s1.text: Around you are people you know personally. Through them you see the people they know: your second and third handshake.

s2.title: A Need travels by handshakes
s2.text: When a participant reports a Need, their people learn of it first, then their people. Everyone decides for themselves whether to take part.

s3.title: Participants agree directly
s3.text: Whoever decides to take part names their amount and joins the chat. Everything else is between people, outside Social Organizer.
